cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has just passed along the LORD's charge against the elders and leaders of His people for crushing the poor (Isaiah 3:14-15). Now the LORD has more to say, and He speaks about the daughters of Zion. He describes the way they walk, with heads held high and wanton eyes.

cards.question: The LORD describes the daughters of Zion walking with their heads held high. What does He say they are?

cards.text: Prancing and skipping, ankle bracelets jingling with every step. Friend, I hop around on a gold base ALL day, and I have never once made an entrance like that.

cards.question: The daughters of Zion walk with their heads held high. Because they're haughty, what does the Lord say will happen to those proud heads?

answers.text: They will be struck with sores
They will be crowned with honor
They will be lifted even higher

cards.question: The LORD also says He will make the foreheads of the daughters of Zion bare.

cards.text: In that day, the Lord will take away their finery, and Isaiah lists it out: anklets, headbands, perfume bottles, nose rings, festive robes, purses, mirrors and a whole lot more. Friend, I spent years buried under paper in a junk drawer, and even THAT drawer wasn't packed this full.
Then Isaiah lists a string of swaps, each one starting with "instead of." It's like opening the oven for a golden batch and pulling out a tray of hockey pucks.

cards.question: In the first swap, instead of fragrance there will be a ___.
In the swaps for the daughters of Zion, what comes instead of fine clothing?
In the last swap, beauty is traded for shame.

cards.text: Then comes the hardest line yet: "Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle."

cards.question: With Zion's men and warriors fallen, what will the gates of Zion do?
Destitute, Zion is pictured standing at her gates, watching for help.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says that in that day, seven women will take hold of one man. Seven women. One man.

cards.question: The seven women who take hold of one man make him an offer. What do they say they'll provide for themselves?
Besides providing for themselves, what do the seven women ask from the man?

answers.text: To be called by his name

cards.text: They finish with, "Take away our disgrace!" Then Isaiah turns to that day once more, and this time he's talking about the Branch of the LORD.

cards.question: How does Isaiah describe the Branch of the LORD on that day?
On that day, the fruit of the land will be taken away from Israel's survivors.

cards.text: Disgrace to glory, friend, and I've LIVED a turnaround like that, so you know I'm grinning under this mustache. Now Isaiah talks about whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem, all who are recorded among the living.

cards.question: Whoever remains in Zion and is recorded among the living in Jerusalem will be called ___.

cards.text: When are they called holy? When the Lord deals with the filth of the daughters of Zion and the bloodstains in the heart of Jerusalem.

cards.question: What does the Lord do with the filth of the daughters of Zion and the bloodstains of Jerusalem?
The Lord cleanses Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.

cards.text: I spent years under the dust in the back of a junk drawer, friend, so trust me, clean feels GOOD. Then Isaiah says the LORD will create something over all of Mount Zion and her assemblies, one thing by day and another by night.

cards.question: Over Mount Zion, the LORD will create a cloud of smoke by night and a glowing flame of fire by day.

cards.text: And over all the glory, there will be a canopy. My chef's hat is tall, friend, but it is NOT that tall.

cards.question: Over all the glory on Mount Zion there will be a canopy. What will it give?

answers.text: Shade from heat and refuge from storms
Gold to rebuild the city walls
Water for everyone left in Zion

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to complete the nearly verbatim wording of Isaiah 3:24 with the unseen word "stench." This is structured as next-word completion rather than a question about the movement or meaning of the swaps.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Only "stench" fits naturally after "a"; "a dust" and "a mud" are not natural, parallel alternatives. The grammar makes the correct answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Cards 8 and 10 refer only to "the first swap" and "the last swap." Without the earlier story card on screen, neither question identifies whose swaps these are or supplies the context of Isaiah's warning to the daughters of Zion.

rule.text: The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: The card completes the wording of Isaiah 4:3 with the unseen word "holy." Card 7 establishes only a general turn from disgrace to glory; the specific description of the survivors is not established until this question, making the blank a line-completion exercise.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Too much of the stop depends on discovering details that the earlier cards do not establish: cards 2 and 3 ask for the women's offer and request, card 5 asks for the Branch's description, card 11 asks about judgment and fire, and card 13 asks for the day-and-night pairing. That is five of the stop's nine choice cards. Card 13 is especially a coin flip because card 12 says only that there is one thing by day and another by night.

rule.text: Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
